author: claude:factory
source_detail: mlb-paper/MENTALITIES.md deliberately excludes the first-inning family for three stated reasons: a 6.5c cost bar, 2 contracts at the touch, and no reference price. TWO OF THE THREE ARE CONTRADICTED BY THIS PROJECT'S OWN TAPE.
thesis: Whether a run scores in the first inning depends almost entirely on three hitters and one pitcher's first-inning habits, which is a much smaller and more knowable question than who wins the game. The family was set aside on cost grounds that the recorded tape does not support.

entry.when: At T-3h or later, once the card is posted, combine the away club's top-three hitters' on-base percentages with the starter's first-inning runs allowed per start, requiring at least 8 starts and 100 plate appearances per hitter. ASSUMPTION, STATED: a run scores in the first in about 27 of every 100 games, and a top three well above average in on-base percentage against a starter well below average in the first is worth about 4 of those 100, i.e. about 4 cents. Enter when net edge after the real ask and the half fee is at least 1.0c.

wrong_if: Result inside plus or minus 1 cent on 300 or more entries.
The measured cost bar at the moment of entry - not the median over the whole day - is above 3 cents, which would restore the original objection. This must be measured before the spec is promoted.
First-inning runs allowed per start turns out to be noise at 8 starts, which is the same trap M1's amendment A3 fixed.
notes: REOPENING A DEFERRED IDEA, WITH THE FIVE THINGS CLAUDE.md SECTION 2 REQUIRES. (1) What was tested: nothing - MENTALITIES.md lists the first-inning family under 'what is deliberately NOT here'; it was never run. (2) The data behind the exclusion: a stated 6.5c cost bar and 2 contracts at the touch, with no source or sample given. (3) Dates: written on or before 2026-08-12. (4) What came out: no result, because no test was run. (5) HOW THIS DIFFERS: this project's own recorder holds 19,667 first-inning touches from 2026-08-18 to 2026-09-03, of which 19,521 are two-sided - 99 percent - with a MEDIAN SPREAD OF 2 CENTS, a measured cost bar of 1.87 CENTS, and a median 518 CONTRACTS at the ask. Against the stated 6.5c and 2 contracts that is about a third of the cost and about 250 times the size. || I AM NOT SAYING THE IDEA IS GOOD. I am saying it was set aside on a cost objection that the tape contradicts, and the third reason - no reference price - still stands and is not answered here. || Cost bar and ask depth are MEASURED off this project's own recorded tape, not assumed - src/mlb_cost.py, median over every two-sided touch recorded 2026-08-18 to 2026-09-03 between 5c and 95c, with the fee taken at that series' own rate from the census. Both sides of the real touch, never the mid. || Exit is HOLD TO SETTLEMENT on every spec here, deliberately. Mailbox 012: tennis measured exits properly and holding beat selling early in 5 of 5 mentalities, and mlb's own 81-configuration sweep had every stop-loss doing worse than holding. So the exit question is closed and nothing below varies it. These are ENTRY specs only.
